Name: Pullman Paris Montparnasse (HOTEL)
Notes: 19 Rue du Commandant René Mouchotte, 75014. +33 1 44 36 44 36. Next to Gare Montparnasse (trains to Versailles-Chantiers). Rooftop bar.

Name: Le Select
Notes: Lost Generation haunt near the hotel. Morning coffee at the bar.

Name: Le Dôme
Notes: Historic art deco brasserie across from Le Select. A drink on the covered terrace; famous for seafood.

Name: Le Rosebud
Notes: 1960s jazz-era cocktail bar on Rue Delambre. Nightcap near the hotel. Opens 6pm.

Name: La Closerie des Lilas
Notes: Hemingway's hangout; famous names engraved on the bar. Drink in the piano bar. Opens noon.

Name: Jardin du Luxembourg
Notes: Grab two green chairs by the fountain and relax.

Name: Café de la Mairie
Notes: Locals' terrace on Place Saint-Sulpice. Coffee or wine; skip the food.

Name: Les Deux Magots
Notes: Famous and pricey but worth it once. Order the hot chocolate.

Name: Café de Flore
Notes: Next door to Deux Magots. Sit on the terrace.

Name: La Palette
Notes: Gallery-street terrace on Rue de Seine. Stick to wine; cocktails are overpriced.

Name: Les Antiquaires
Notes: Corner bistro two blocks from Orsay. Coffee before or lunch after.

Name: Musée d'Orsay
Notes: Book timed ticket. Closed Mondays. Start on the 5th floor (Impressionists).

Name: Musée de l'Orangerie
Notes: Monet's Water Lilies. Book timed ticket. Closed Tuesdays. About 1 hour.

Name: Arc de Triomphe
Notes: Option B afternoon: rooftop views + Champs-Élysées. Covered by the museum pass, walk-in. Use the underground tunnel to reach it.

Name: Sainte-Chapelle
Notes: Book timed ticket: 3:30pm (option A) or 9:30am (option B). Morning light is best.

Name: Notre-Dame de Paris
Notes: Free entry. Reserve a free time slot online to skip the main line.

Name: Le Saint-Régis
Notes: Just over the bridge on Île Saint-Louis. Coffee stop after Notre-Dame.

Name: Berthillon
Notes: Best sorbet in Paris. Closed Mon & Tue.

Name: Benoit
Notes: RESERVE Sunday dinner 7:30pm. 1912 bistro, open daily 12-2 and 7-10pm. Get the profiteroles.

Name: Eiffel Tower
Notes: Dinner with the friends (already arranged). The tower sparkles on the hour after dark. Watch for pickpockets.

Name: Rue Cler
Notes: HIGHLIGHT. Pedestrian market street: cheese shops, bakeries, produce, flowers. Best Tue-Sat; most shops closed Mon, quiet Sun afternoon.

Name: Café du Marché
Notes: The Rue Cler café. Terrace lunch and people-watching.

Name: Napoleon's Tomb (Invalides)
Notes: 10 min walk from Rue Cler. About an hour for the dome.

Name: Le Nemours
Notes: Terrace under the Palais-Royal arcades steps from the Louvre. Coffee before / recovery after.

Name: Louvre
Notes: Book earliest timed slot. Closed Tuesdays. Pick 3-4 must-sees.

Name: Le Rubis
Notes: Old-school zinc wine bar full of regulars. Chalkboard menu. Closed Sunday.

Name: Willi's Wine Bar
Notes: Paris wine-bar institution since 1980. Great early dinner. Closed Sunday.

Name: Le Baron Rouge
Notes: Standing-room wine bar by the Aligre market. Pre-dinner glass; 10 min walk to Paul Bert.

Name: Bistrot Paul Bert
Notes: RESERVE (call ~10:30am or 4pm Paris time). Steak au poivre. Closed Sun & Mon.

Name: Marché Edgar-Quinet
Notes: WED & SAT mornings (7am-1:30/2:30pm). 5 min walk from hotel. Rotisserie chicken + oysters.

Name: Marché Raspail
Notes: TUE & FRI mornings; SUNDAY is the famous organic market. Near Luxembourg.

Name: Poilâne
Notes: THE legendary bread bakery. Get a slice of the big P loaf, the apple tart, and the butter cookies. Closed Sun.

Name: Pierre Hermé
Notes: Best macarons in Paris. Try the Ispahan (rose/raspberry/lychee). Takeaway only.

Name: La Grande Épicerie de Paris
Notes: Gorgeous gourmet food hall. Butter, cheese, gifts to bring home; big wine cellar downstairs. Open daily.

Name: Fromagerie Quatrehomme
Notes: Top cheesemonger; staff will pick for you and vacuum-pack for the flight. Closed Mon.

Name: La Dernière Goutte
Notes: Tiny, friendly wine shop; owner speaks English and loves recommending bottles. Great Burgundy.

Name: Barthélémy
Notes: Classic old cheese shop ~10 min walk from Orsay. Vacuum-packs for travel. Closed Sun & Mon.

Name: La Maison d'Isabelle
Notes: Award-winning croissant, just across the bridge from Notre-Dame. Short line moves fast. Closed Mon.

Name: Fromagerie Laurent Dubois
Notes: Next door to Isabelle. Ask to taste the aged Comté. Closed Mon.

Name: Marché Maubert
Notes: TUE, THU & SAT mornings. Small, local market 5 min from Notre-Dame.

Name: Marché aux Fleurs
Notes: Flower market between Sainte-Chapelle and Notre-Dame. Open daily.

Name: Marché Saxe-Breteuil
Notes: THU & SAT mornings. Big, beautiful market with the Eiffel Tower in view. Go before 11.

Name: Marie-Anne Cantin
Notes: Top cheese shop right off Rue Cler; ask for a 5-cheese tasting plate for a Champ de Mars picnic. Closed Mon.

Name: Stohrer
Notes: Oldest pastry shop in Paris (1730) on the Rue Montorgueil market street, ~15 min from the Louvre. Get the baba au rhum.

Name: Legrand Filles et Fils
Notes: Historic wine shop + tasting bar in Galerie Vivienne, steps from Palais-Royal. Closed Sun.

Name: Marché d'Aligre
Notes: TUE-SUN mornings (closed Mon); busiest Sat & Sun. Outdoor stalls + covered hall + flea market. Morning trip, separate from dinner.

Name: Blé Sucré
Notes: Locals' pick for croissant and pain au chocolat, right by Aligre. Closed Mon.

Name: Palace of Versailles
Notes: CLOSED MON. Book timed tickets ahead; take earliest slot. Train from Gare Montparnasse to Versailles-Chantiers (~15 min) then ~20 min walk or taxi.

Name: Marché Notre-Dame (Versailles)
Notes: Outdoor market TUE, FRI & SUN mornings; covered halls open Tue-Sun. Build a picnic for the palace gardens.
